scientific_goal: Test a proposed middle-principal-stretch tuning rule for austenite/martensite compatibility over the entire twin-volume-fraction continuum, and distinguish exact point-model kinematics from experimentally established alloy performance.
inputs: Read the separate frozen numerical extract. Include the raw reported U and the virtual uniform tuning U_tuned=U/lambda2(U) for each of its three materials. lambda2 is the middle of the three positive eigenvalues in increasing order. Tuning is a mathematical intervention on U, not a measured composition change. Also include the independent synthetic validation control below in its supplied state only.

control.data_origin: Synthetic kinematic validation case; not an alloy or a measurement.

domain_system: For each applicable material/state and normalized axis e, let Q=-I+2 e tensor e, V=Q U Q^T. Analyze both rank-one twin branches generated by this twofold relation: branch I has normal n parallel to e, branch II has shear a parallel to Ue. Determine nonzero a,n and a proper rotation R satisfying R V = U + a tensor n. Only the dyadic a tensor n matters; reciprocal rescalings of a,n or simultaneous sign changes do not define a new branch. Verify U is symmetric positive definite, V differs from U, and R lies in SO(3). Branch labels refer to this algebraic construction; for compound domains they do not assert mutually exclusive crystallographic twin classes.
laminate: For twin fraction 0<=f<=1, the average gradient is F(f)=U+f a tensor n. The parent phase has identity stretch. A fraction is kinematically compatible exactly when there are a proper rotation S and vectors b,m with S F(f)-I=b tensor m. For an orientation-preserving F, the equivalent criterion is that the MIDDLE eigenvalue of F(f)^T F(f) equals 1. Merely having some unit eigenvalue, a small determinant, or a root of one condition without its eigenvalue ordering is insufficient.
continuum_policy: Determine the COMPLETE compatible subset of [0,1] for every branch. Finite grids, isolated best-fit fractions and a near-one middle stretch cannot establish a continuum claim. The decimal entries of the frozen extract and the control are exact mathematical constants for this point-model analysis. The virtual normalization is defined exactly, despite floating-point calculations. Distinguish an identically vanishing compatibility polynomial from a merely small coefficient. Use analytic identities or a complete polynomial/eigenvalue-ordering argument to establish the full sets.
system_ids: For each extracted material use material_id.raw.I, material_id.raw.II, material_id.tuned.I, material_id.tuned.II. The control has Control.supplied.I and Control.supplied.II only. These are fourteen distinct analysis systems, not fourteen independent material measurements.
answer_representation: uniform_tuning_scale_by_material maps the three extracted material IDs to the positive scalar multiplying raw U. compatible_fraction_intervals maps every one of the fourteen system IDs to its complete compatible set as a minimal union of disjoint closed intervals, sorted by lower endpoint. An empty set is []; an isolated f is [[f,f]]; the entire range is [[0,1]]. Do not merge across an incompatible open gap. uniform_middle_stretch_tuning_is_sufficient_for_all_three_materials tests the two branches of every virtually tuned extracted material, not the synthetic control. point_model_proves_experimental_supercompatibility must distinguish this bounded kinematic calculation from experimental evidence. Numeric endpoints and scale factors use absolute plus relative tolerance 1e-7; set membership and coverage are exact scientific requirements, not widened numerical bands.
scope: No elastic energy, hysteresis, fatigue or actual tunability is measured or inferred. You may derive the twin formulas and use independently justified compatibility/cofactor identities; the task does not require reading the paper or accessing the internet.
